title: Superposition Density of Safety vs. Capability Features: Is Safety Under-Resourced in the Residual Stream?

novelty_assessment.label: mostly_novel
novelty_assessment.reasoning: While SAEs for interpretability are well-established (Cunningham et al. 2023, Anthropic's monosemanticity work, OpenAI's scaling SAEs), and safety neurons have been studied (Chen et al. 2024 'Safety Neurons' NeurIPS 2025), the specific question of whether safety-relevant features are under-resourced in superposition relative to capability features has not been directly investigated. The 'Safety Neurons' paper found safety and helpfulness neurons overlap (~5% of neurons) but did not frame this as a superposition density comparison. The idea of measuring relative feature density and suppression susceptibility of safety vs capability features in SAE-decomposed representations is a novel angle on an active research area.

title: The Capability-Safety Tradeoff Circuit: Identifying Heads That Are Jointly Responsible for Both

novelty_assessment.label: partially_addressed

(2024) 'Towards Understanding Safety Alignment: A Mechanistic Perspective from Safety Neurons' (NeurIPS 2025) already identified that safety and helpfulness neurons are highly overlapped, providing a mechanistic interpretation of the alignment tax. Their work uses activation contrasting and dynamic activation patching to locate ~5% safety neurons and show overlap with helpfulness. The proposed idea of head-level ablation across dual benchmarks and Pareto tradeoff mapping is a complementary methodology, but the core finding — that safety and capability share overlapping components — is substantially established. The head-level (vs neuron-level) granularity and activation steering on overlapping heads add some novelty.

title: Instruction-Following vs. Safety-Following: When These Circuits Conflict, Which Wins?

novelty_assessment.label: partially_addressed

They found that conflict signals are encoded early with high separability but the model lacks a stable rule to prefer safety. Additionally, the 'Jailbreaks Peak Early Then Drop' work on LessWrong studied layer-wise trajectories of how jailbreak signals interact with safety circuits. The specific framing of residual-stream magnitude competition between instruction-following and safety circuits adds a mechanistic angle not fully covered, but the behavioral and representational findings are substantially established.

title: Lying About Reasoning: Do Chain-of-Thought Reasoning Tokens Reflect Internal Computation or Post-Hoc Confabulation?

novelty_assessment.label: largely_addressed
novelty_assessment.reasoning: This question has been substantially investigated. 'Chain-of-Thought Is Not Explainability' (Barez et al., Oxford/WhiteBox 2025) established that CoT frequently diverges from actual computations, with larger models being less faithful. 'How does Chain of Thought Think? Mechanistic Interpretability of Chain-of-Thought Reasoning with Sparse Autoencoding' (arXiv:2507.22928, 2025) used SAEs and activation patching to study CoT faithfulness mechanistically. 'Unfaithful Explanations in Chain-of-Thought Prompting' (Alignment Forum) demonstrated systematic confabulation. Multiple works have identified the 'answer-first' failure mode where models decide answers before generating reasoning. The specific methodology of patching the answer-commitment layer and measuring CoT change is partially novel, but the core finding — CoT is often confabulated — is well-established with mechanistic evidence.

title: Factual Confidence vs. Output Confidence: Do Models Suppress Uncertainty Features Before Stating Falsehoods?

title: Consistency Training and Circuit Hardening: Does Consistency Training Strengthen the Refusal Feature?

novelty_assessment.label: mostly_novel
novelty_assessment.reasoning: While the refusal direction is well-established (Arditi et al. 2024, NeurIPS), and methods to harden it exist (ROSI: Rank-One Safety Injection, arXiv:2508.20766), the specific question of whether consistency training as a training objective strengthens the refusal feature's magnitude and geometry has not been directly studied. ROSI injects refusal directions post-hoc without training; the proposed idea instead asks whether a training-time consistency objective naturally amplifies the refusal feature. This is a distinct and novel experimental question. The pre/post SAE-level measurement of refusal feature geometry under consistency training is unexplored territory.

title: Sparse Autoencoder Feature Stability Under Fine-Tuning: Do Safety Features Survive Safety-Irrelevant Fine-Tuning?

novelty_assessment.label: mostly_novel

Safe-SAIL (arXiv:2509.18127) maps safety features but does not study their stability under fine-tuning. The SAE feature transferability work (EMNLP 2025) studied cross-model transfer but not within-model fine-tuning stability. This is a novel experimental design with practical implications for understanding safety degradation.

title: Measuring SAE Feature Sensitivity Decay Across Distribution Shifts

novelty_assessment.label: already_solved
novelty_assessment.reasoning: This idea is directly addressed by 'Measuring Sparse Autoencoder Feature Sensitivity' (arXiv:2509.23717, OpenReview 2025). That paper introduces a scalable method to evaluate feature sensitivity — how reliably a feature activates on texts similar to its activating examples — using LM-generated paraphrases. Key findings include: many interpretable features have poor sensitivity, sensitivity declines with increasing SAE width, and sensitivity measures a new facet of feature quality distinct from interpretability. The proposed methodology (sample 200 features, collect top activating examples, generate paraphrases, measure activation fraction, compare across layers/frequency/width) is almost exactly the methodology of the published paper.

title: Characterizing the Dead Feature Problem in Narrow vs. Wide SAEs

novelty_assessment.label: partially_addressed
novelty_assessment.reasoning: The dead feature problem is well-documented in SAE literature. OpenAI's 'Scaling and Evaluating Sparse Autoencoders' (arXiv:2406.04093, 2024) characterized dead features at scale and proposed k-sparse autoencoders that reduce dead latents. Anthropic's monosemanticity work discusses dead neuron resampling. Deep sparse autoencoders (LessWrong 2025) showed that optimizer choice (Muon/Signum) and linear k-decay schedules fix dead neurons. However, a systematic characterization specifically comparing dead feature rates and properties across narrow vs wide SAEs as a focused empirical study, with the specific metrics proposed, has not been published as a standalone study. The engineering knowledge is scattered across larger papers rather than being the central contribution.

title: Where Do Attribution Graphs Fail? Identifying Prompt Classes Where Circuit Tracing Breaks Down
